headings.title: Contracts to terminate water service for nonpayment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sewer corporations, municipalities, and statutory or constitutional sewer districts to contract with water providers to shut off water service for unpaid sewer bills after thirty days notice.

headings.title: Water provider liability immunity and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil immunity to water providers terminating water service under contract absent negligence and requires sewer entities to indemnify water providers and reimburse termination costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Contracts between sewer entities and water providers to discontinue water service for unpaid sewer bills, with notice requirements, liability protections, and expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Mandatory contract upon sewer provider request
headings.reviewNote: Directs municipal water providers and public water supply districts to contract with sewer providers upon request to terminate water service for delinquent sewer bills.

headings.title: Civil liability exemption for water providers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts water providers and their independent contractors acting under contract from all civil liability arising from termination of water services.

headings.title: Petition for appointment of commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sewer providers to petition the circuit court to select three commissioners if no contract is reached within six months of request.

headings.title: Required terms of water shutoff agreement
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory terms for shutoff agreements, including equal delinquency thresholds, written notice, liability insurance, and reimbursement of disconnection costs.

headings.title: Selection and appointment of commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Establishes procedures and timelines for the selection of three commissioners by the sewer provider, water provider, and circuit court.

headings.title: Drafting of agreement and party hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires commissioners to hold a hearing on fifteen days written notice to each party and submit a drafted agreement to the court within ninety days.

headings.title: Court review and approval of agreement
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the circuit court to approve, reject, or require modifications to the commissioners agreement, making it effective sixty days after judgment.

headings.title: Appeal rights and assessment of costs
headings.reviewNote: Provides for appeal of court judgments approving agreements and taxes all costs and expert witness fees to the requesting sewer provider.

headings.title: Exempted municipalities and charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Exempts any city not within a county and any charter county with more than one million inhabitants from the provisions of this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory agreements between water and sewer providers to terminate water service for unpaid sewer charges, appointment of commissioners upon impasse, agreement terms, and judicial review.

headings.title: Eminent domain authority of sewer corporations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sewer corporations to acquire lands, property, and rights through eminent domain in the manner prescribed for gas and electrical corporations.

headings.title: Placement of sewer lines along public roads
headings.reviewNote: Permits sewer corporations to construct pipes along, across, or under public roads, streets, and waters without incommoding the public, subject to municipal consent within municipalities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authority of sewer corporations to exercise eminent domain and construct sewer pipes along or across public rights-of-way with municipal consent.

headings.title: Water appropriation and condemnation rights
headings.reviewNote: Grants water corporations the right to take water from nonnavigable streams, erect dams, and condemn land for pipelines, well drilling, and water management facilities.

headings.title: Circuit court petition for condemnation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes application to the circuit court by petition stating the desired property rights when agreement on compensation cannot be reached with landowners.

entries.reviewSummary: Rights of water suppliers to take water from nonnavigable streams, erect dams, and condemn land for pipelines and facilities, and procedure for petitioning circuit court.

headings.title: Petition filing and issuance of summons
headings.reviewNote: Requires the circuit judge upon receiving a water condemnation petition to order it filed and issue summons giving landowners at least ten days notice served by the sheriff.

headings.title: Service of notice by publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice by newspaper publication for three consecutive weeks, or courthouse door posting if no newspaper exists, for unknown or nonresident landowners.

entries.reviewSummary: Notice and summons requirements upon filing of condemnation petition by water suppliers, including publication notice for absent or unknown landowners.

headings.title: Appointment of commissioners and assessment of damages
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to appoint three disinterested commissioners to assess damages, report under oath, and allows utility possession upon payment or abandonment within ten days.

headings.title: Inquiry and report on stream usage damages
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commissioners or jury to determine damages for stream diversion or dam construction and permits interested parties to appear and file exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Appointment of commissioners to assess damages for land appropriation and stream diversion, payment of damages, right of abandonment, and filing of exceptions.

headings.title: Infrastructure system replacement surcharge petition in charter county
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes water corporations in charter counties with over one million inhabitants to petition for an infrastructure system replacement surcharge (ISRS) between one million dollars and ten percent of base revenue.

headings.title: General rate proceeding order prerequisite
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits commission approval of an ISRS unless the water corporation has had a general rate proceeding decided or dismissed within the past three years or has a pending proceeding.

headings.title: Three-year limit on surcharge collection
headings.reviewNote: Restricts ISRS collections to a maximum period of three years unless the water corporation has filed for or is subject to a new general rate proceeding.

entries.reviewSummary: Authority of water corporations in charter counties with over one million inhabitants to petition for an infrastructure system replacement surcharge (ISRS) and timing limitations.

headings.title: Submission of ISRS rate schedules and notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires a water corporation filing an ISRS petition to submit supporting documentation, serve the public counsel, and directs the commission to publish notice.

headings.title: Commission examination, hearing, and report and order
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission examination of the petition, permits commission staff to submit a report within sixty days, allows a hearing, and requires an order effective within one hundred twenty days.

headings.title: Limit on frequency of ISRS rate changes
headings.reviewNote: Limits a water corporation to effectuating a change in its ISRS rate no more often than two times every twelve months.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining pretax revenues
headings.reviewNote: Restricts commission determination of appropriate pretax revenues to seven enumerated factors including tax rates, capital structure, debt and equity costs, property taxes, depreciation, and rate-case testimony fallback.

headings.title: ISRS calculation, allocation, and annual reconciliation
headings.reviewNote: Governs calculating and prorating ISRS surcharges by customer-class benefit and billing determinants, and requires annual reconciliation of ISRS revenues against appropriate pretax revenues.

headings.title: Reset of surcharge upon new base rates
headings.reviewNote: Mandates resetting the ISRS rate to zero when new base rates become effective following a general rate proceeding and reconciling unreconciled revenues.

headings.title: General rate increase distinction
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that filing an ISRS petition or modification does not constitute a request for a general increase in base rates and charges.

headings.title: Effect of general rate proceeding on prudence
headings.reviewNote: Provides that commission approval of an ISRS is not binding on prudence determinations in subsequent general rate proceedings and requires offsets for disallowed costs.

headings.title: Commission general rate authority preserved
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that ISRS provisions do not limit commission authority to review infrastructure replacement costs in general rate proceedings or review rates under section 386.390.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to promulgate rules implementing the water ISRS provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures, documentation, commission review, rate change frequency limit, pretax revenue factors, calculation and annual reconciliation, base rate resets, prudence reviews, and rulemaking authority for water ISRS.

headings.title: Petition to establish gas infrastructure surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes gas corporations to petition the commission for an ISRS rate schedule to recover eligible infrastructure system replacement costs, subject to revenue limits and commission refund orders.

headings.title: General rate proceeding prerequisite for approval
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits commission approval of an ISRS for a gas corporation that has not had a general rate proceeding decided or dismissed within the preceding three years unless a new proceeding is pending.

headings.title: Maximum collection period without rate proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits collecting an ISRS for more than three years unless the gas corporation has filed for or is subject to a new general rate proceeding.

headings.title: Contractor prequalification and competitive bidding requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires gas corporations to develop a contractor prequalification process and competitively bid at least twenty-five percent of external installation expenditures for ISRS projects.

headings.title: Annual commission report on competitive bidding
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to submit an annual report to the general assembly starting December 31, 2023, regarding gas corporation compliance and costs under competitive bidding requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Gas corporation infrastructure system replacement surcharge petition eligibility, rate proceeding prerequisites, competitive contractor bidding requirements, and annual reporting to the general assembly.

headings.title: Filing of proposed ISRS rate schedules
headings.reviewNote: Requires a gas corporation to submit proposed ISRS schedules and supporting documentation with its petition, serve public counsel, and directs commission publication of notice.

headings.title: Commission examination, staff report, and order
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission examination of the petition, permits commission staff to report within ninety days, allows a hearing, and requires an order effective within one hundred eighty days.

headings.title: Limit on frequency of ISRS rate changes
headings.reviewNote: Limits a gas corporation to effectuating a change in its ISRS rate no more often than two times every twelve months.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining pretax revenue
headings.reviewNote: Restricts commission determination of appropriate pretax revenue to seven enumerated factors including tax rates, capital structure, debt and equity costs, property taxes, depreciation, and rate-case testimony fallback.

headings.title: Monthly ISRS calculation and annual reconciliation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes calculating monthly ISRS charges by customer numbers or proportional customer-class charges, and requires annual reconciliation of ISRS revenues against appropriate pretax revenues.

headings.title: Reset of surcharge upon new base rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires resetting the ISRS surcharge to zero when new base rates take effect after a general rate case and reconciling remaining balances.

headings.title: General rate increase distinction
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that filing an ISRS petition or change does not constitute a request for a general rate increase.

headings.title: Prudence review in subsequent rate proceeding
headings.reviewNote: States that ISRS approval is not binding on prudence determinations in subsequent general rate cases and requires offsets for any disallowed costs.

headings.title: General rate proceeding authority preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves commission authority to review and evaluate infrastructure costs during general rate proceedings.

headings.title: Rate reasonableness inquiry preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves commission authority to investigate the reasonableness of gas rates and prudence of infrastructure investments under section 386.390.

headings.title: Promulgation of implementation rules
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to implement gas ISRS provisions subject to nonseverability under chapter 536.

headings.title: Customer refunds for unlawful charges
headings.reviewNote: Mandates complete customer refunds of any ISRS charges found unlawful or inappropriate by a court prior to filing any new ISRS petition.

headings.title: Expiration of gas infrastructure surcharge sections
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of August 28, 2029, for sections 393.1009 to 393.1015.

entries.reviewSummary: Gas corporation ISRS petition procedures, ninety-day staff report and one-hundred-eighty-day order deadlines, rate change limits, pretax revenue factors, monthly calculation and reconciliation, prudence reviews, customer refunds, and August 28, 2029 expiration date.

headings.title: Renewable energy portfolio requirement percentages
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes renewable energy portfolio requirements ramping from two percent in 2011 to fifteen percent by 2021, with at least two percent from solar energy and bonus credit for Missouri generation.

headings.title: Accelerated renewable buyer exemption and criteria
headings.reviewNote: Establishes exemptions from utility renewable standard compliance costs for accelerated renewable buyers with aggregate load over eighty average megawatts who retire renewable energy certificates.

headings.title: REC tracking, rate cap, penalties, and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Requires selecting a renewable energy credit tracking program with three-year credit life and adopting enforcement rules including a one percent maximum average retail rate increase cap, noncompliance penalties, annual reports, and cost recovery.

headings.title: Customer solar rebates and tariff suspension
headings.reviewNote: Requires nonexempt electric utilities to offer customer solar rebates up to twenty-five kilowatts ramping from two dollars per watt through June 30, 2014, to zero after June 30, 2020, with tariff suspension if the one percent cap is reached and ten-year REC transfer.

headings.title: Department certification of renewable generation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to certify eligible renewable energy resources and verify electricity generated or purchased by electric utilities.

headings.title: Animal waste methane and waste-to-energy resources
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission and department to include methane from anaerobic digestion of farm animal waste and thermal depolymerization or pyrolysis converting waste material to energy as renewable energy resources.

headings.title: Commission rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to promulgate consistent implementation rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2013.

entries.reviewSummary: Renewable energy portfolio requirements for electric utilities, accelerated renewable buyer exemptions, REC tracking and enforcement rules with one percent rate cap, customer solar rebates, department certification, biogas/pyrolysis inclusion, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Agreement waiving partition or restricting alienation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electrical or gas corporations holding joint or co-tenancy ownership in utility property to agree to waive partition rights or restrict alienation until abandonment of use.

headings.title: Perpetuities and restraint on alienation rules inapplicable
headings.reviewNote: Declares the rule against perpetuities and the rule against unreasonable restraints on alienation inapplicable to joint utility ownership agreements entered into under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorization for jointly owned electric or gas facilities to restrict alienation or waive partition, and exemption from the rule against perpetuities and unreasonable restraints on alienation.

headings.title: Definitions of electric service and structure terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines auxiliary power, independent power producer (IPP), permanent service, and structure for electric supplier service rights.

headings.title: Exclusive right to provide electric service
headings.reviewNote: Grants electrical corporations and joint municipal utility commissions exclusive rights to continue serving structures through permanent facilities, and authorizes PSC change-of-supplier orders in the public interest for reasons other than a rate differential.

headings.title: Wholesale auxiliary power purchase by qualifying IPP
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wholesale purchase of auxiliary power under federal RTO tariffs for an IPP generation facility in a qualifying first-class county operating prior to August 28, 2021, noting the source footnote that 'chapters' appears in original rolls of H.B. 734, 2021.

headings.title: Service to replacement structure in former rural area
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a retail electric supplier serving a structure in a municipality that ceased to be a rural area to serve a new replacement structure upon owner request, noting the source footnote on original roll wording in H.B. 271 and H.B. 734, 2021.

entries.reviewSummary: Definitions, exclusive rights of electric suppliers to serve existing structures and PSC change-of-supplier authority, wholesale auxiliary power for qualifying IPPs, and replacement structure service in former rural areas.

headings.title: Establishment and membership of solar taxation task force
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Task Force on Fair, Nondiscriminatory Local Taxation Concerning Solar Energy Systems and designates its fifteen legislative, county assessor, agency, agricultural, solar industry, and advocacy members.

headings.title: Public hearings, research, and report contents
headings.reviewNote: Directs the task force to hold public hearings and compile a report to the general assembly before December 31, 2022, regarding uniform solar energy system assessment and taxation.

headings.title: Organization, officers, meetings, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Specifies organizational requirements for task force meetings, selection of chair and vice chair, recordkeeping, and quorum voting.

headings.title: Research and clerical staff assistance
headings.reviewNote: Directs house research and senate research staff to provide necessary clerical, research, fiscal, and legal support services to the task force.

headings.title: Member expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that task force members serve without compensation but shall be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Expiration of task force section
headings.reviewNote: Provides for the expiration of the task force section on December 31, 2022.

entries.reviewSummary: Creation, membership, duties, reporting requirements, organization, and December 31, 2022 expiration of the task force on fair local taxation concerning solar energy systems.

headings.title: Citation as Missouri Energy Efficiency Investment Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates this section as the Missouri Energy Efficiency Investment Act.

headings.title: Definitions of demand-side and efficiency terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission, demand response, demand-side program, energy efficiency, interruptible or curtailable rate, and total resource cost test.

headings.title: State policy valuing demand-side investments equally
headings.reviewNote: Establishes state policy valuing demand-side investments equal to supply and delivery investments and directs the commission to provide timely cost recovery, aligned financial incentives, and timely earnings opportunities.

headings.title: Program approval and total resource cost test
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission approval of demand-side programs beneficial to all class customers with the total resource cost test preferred, exempting low-income and general education programs found in the public interest.

headings.title: Cost recovery mechanisms and class apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes demand-side cost recovery mechanisms including capitalization, rate design modifications after docket and rulemaking, accelerated depreciation, and shared net benefits, with fair apportionment across customer classes.

headings.title: Low-income subclass allocation reduction or exemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to reduce or exempt allocation of demand-side expenditures to low-income residential subclasses defined in a rate proceeding.

headings.title: Large customer opt-out from program charges
headings.reviewNote: Allows large electric customers meeting demand thresholds of 5,000 kW, aggregate 2,500 kW, or interstate pipeline pumping stations to opt out of demand-side charges.

headings.title: Reentry restrictions after customer opt-out
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits customers who opt out of demand-side programs from subsequently participating except under guidelines established by commission rules.

headings.title: Program funding commitment upon customer participation
headings.reviewNote: Requires customers participating in demand-side programs initiated after August 1, 2009, to fund programs for a period set by commission rule.

headings.title: Continued eligibility for interruptible rate schedules
headings.reviewNote: Ensures customers electing not to participate in demand-side programs remain eligible for interruptible or curtailable rate schedules.

headings.title: Commission oversight and rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to oversee demand-side programs, adopt rules and procedures, and approve utility tariffs and settlements subject to chapter 536 nonseverability.

headings.title: Annual utility report on demand-side programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires each electrical corporation to submit an annual report documenting demand-side program expenditures, peak demand reductions, energy savings, and net economic benefits.

headings.title: Separate line-item billing for program charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires charges attributable to demand-side programs under this section to appear as a distinct line item on customer utility bills.

headings.title: Disclosure rules for monetary incentive recipients
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to promulgate rules requiring disclosure of participants who receive monetary incentives under demand-side programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Missouri Energy Efficiency Investment Act establishing definitions, equal valuation policy, demand-side program approval, cost recovery mechanisms, low-income exemptions, large customer opt-out rules, oversight, annual reporting, and participant disclosure.

headings.title: Annual capacity obligation documentation requirement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to require electrical corporations to submit annual documentation demonstrating sufficient capacity for the upcoming planning year and three subsequent years.

headings.title: Additional audits and capacity reporting authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to require audits and reporting to determine whether an electrical corporation has secured sufficient capacity for planning years four years out.

headings.title: Cost disallowance for imprudent capacity failure
headings.reviewNote: Allows the commission to disallow costs after hearing and order remediation plans if an electrical corporation imprudently fails to maintain sufficient capacity.

headings.title: Definitions of regional transmission organization and sufficient capacity
headings.reviewNote: Defines appropriate regional transmission organization or independent system operator, electrical corporation, and sufficient capacity.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the commission to implement capacity obligation provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for electrical corporations to submit annual capacity obligation documentation, commission audit authority, disallowances for imprudent capacity deficits, and definitions.

headings.title: Scope and application of statutory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that sections 393.110 to 393.285 apply to gas, electric, water, and sewer utilities furnishing service for light, heat, power, water supply, or sewage disposal.

headings.title: Public service commission jurisdiction exemption for cooperatives
headings.reviewNote: Exempts nonprofit cooperative electrical corporations serving member-stockholders in third class counties from commission jurisdiction over rates, financing, accounting, and management.

entries.reviewSummary: Application of sections 393.110 to 393.285 to gas, electric, water, and sewer utilities, and exemption of certain nonprofit cooperative electrical corporations from commission jurisdiction.

headings.title: Safe and adequate service and reasonable charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires gas, electric, water, and sewer corporations to provide safe, adequate, and reasonable service facilities and mandates that all charges be just and reasonable.

headings.title: Prohibition on unjust discrimination and rebates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public utilities from charging discriminatory rates, offering rebates, or collecting unequal compensation for like services under substantially similar circumstances.

headings.title: Prohibition on unreasonable preferences or advantages
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public utilities from granting undue or unreasonable preference or advantage to any person, corporation, or locality, or subjecting them to prejudice or disadvantage.

headings.title: Sliding scale for automatic charge adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Permits commission-approved fixed-period sliding scales for automatic adjustment of utility charges and stockholder dividends while preserving commission rate-fixing authority after expiration, noting the footnote that section 393.285 was repealed in 1999.

headings.title: Prohibition on municipal fire hydrant charges
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits water corporations from charging municipalities or fire protection districts for placing and providing fire hydrants, while allowing placement and maintenance costs in the water rate cost basis.

headings.title: Interest accrual on municipal water and sewer deposits
headings.reviewNote: Requires home rule cities with over four hundred thousand inhabitants in more than one county to accrue six-month U.S. Treasury bill interest on water and sewerage deposits held two or more years for current customers.

headings.title: Service tariff schedules for large electric customers
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations with over 250,000 customers to submit service tariff schedules for customers projected at 100 MW or more peak demand (50 MW or more for smaller utilities as of January 1, 2025) and authorizes similar commission orders for lower demands.

entries.reviewSummary: Utility requirements for safe and adequate service, just and reasonable rates, bans on discrimination and preferences, sliding scale rates, fire hydrant charge ban, municipal utility deposit interest, and large electric load tariffs.

headings.title: Prohibition on nonoperational property and CWIP charges
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits electrical corporations from demanding charges based on construction in progress or nonoperational property before it is fully operational and used for service.

headings.title: Construction work in progress for gas generating units
headings.reviewNote: Permits electrical corporations to include construction work in progress for new natural gas-generating units in rate base subject to refund with section 32.065 interest and contingent expiration on December 31, 2035 unless extended through December 31, 2045.

entries.reviewSummary: General prohibition against utility charges based on construction work in progress or nonoperational property, with exception for new natural gas-generating units expiring in 2035.

headings.title: Applicability to electrical corporations without pending rate case
headings.reviewNote: Applies section provisions to electrical corporations without a general rate proceeding pending as of February 1, 2018, or June 1, 2018.

headings.title: Definitions of commission and electrical corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission and electrical corporation for the purposes of rate adjustments under this section.

headings.title: One-time rate adjustment reflecting 2017 tax act
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to make a one-time adjustment to electric utility rates reflecting the 2017 federal Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and defer financial impacts to a regulatory asset.

headings.title: Alternative regulatory asset deferral upon good cause
headings.reviewNote: Permits the commission upon good cause shown to allow alternative deferral of 2017 federal tax act impacts to a regulatory asset through the next general rate proceeding, noting the source footnote that '2' appears in original rolls for subsection 3.

entries.reviewSummary: One-time rate adjustment and regulatory asset deferral mechanism for electrical corporations reflecting the federal Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017.

headings.title: Definitions of commission and electrical corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission and electrical corporation for the purposes of corporate income tax rate adjustments under this section.

headings.title: One-time rate adjustment for federal corporate tax reduction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a one-time rate adjustment and regulatory asset deferral if federal corporate income tax rates are reduced between January 20, 2025, and December 31, 2029.

headings.title: Alternative deferral to regulatory asset upon public interest
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission upon a public interest finding to allow alternative deferral of tax reduction impacts to a regulatory asset through the next general rate proceeding.

entries.reviewSummary: One-time rate adjustment authority and regulatory asset deferral procedures for electrical corporations if federal corporate income tax rates are reduced between 2025 and 2029.

headings.title: Definitions of qualifying electric plant and rate terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission, electrical corporation, qualifying electric plant, rate-base cutoff date, and weighted average cost of capital.

headings.title: Deferral of depreciation expense to regulatory asset
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing electrical corporations to defer eighty-five percent of depreciation expense and return on qualifying electric plant to a regulatory asset for rate-base inclusion subject to prudence disallowances, carrying costs, and twenty-year amortization.

headings.title: Calculation of deferred depreciation and return
headings.reviewNote: Specifies calculation of deferred depreciation net of replaced plant retirements and deferred return using weighted average cost of capital plus taxes, accounting for accumulated deferred income taxes and accumulated depreciation.

headings.title: Five-year capital investment and grid modernization plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual five-year capital investment plans by February 28, cost-benefit quantification for projects over twenty million dollars, a six percent smart meter cap for five years, at least twenty-five percent grid modernization spending, stakeholder meetings, and prior-year investment reports.

headings.title: Election notice, deferral period, and five-year extension
headings.reviewNote: Requires written election notice, bars concurrent use with section 386.266(3) adjustments, authorizes deferrals through December 31, 2035 with a possible five-year extension upon application by December 31, 2033, and applies section 393.1656 caps from January 1, 2024.

headings.title: Business risk consideration in allowed return
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to take into account any change in business risk resulting from implementation of the deferrals when setting the corporation's allowed return in any rate proceeding.

headings.title: Expiration date and continuation of regulatory assets
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of December 31, 2040, while preserving the right to recover remaining regulatory asset balances and continue amortization.

entries.reviewSummary: Deferral of eighty-five percent of depreciation expense and return on qualifying electric plant to a regulatory asset, annual five-year capital investment and grid modernization plans, election rules, business risk adjustments, and December 31, 2040 expiration.

headings.title: Petition for receivership of small water or sewer utility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission after hearing to petition Cole County or local circuit court to attach assets and appoint a receiver for a water or sewer corporation serving 8,000 or fewer connections that is unable or unwilling to provide safe service, abandoned, or in state debt default.

headings.title: Appointment and authority of interim receiver
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to appoint a compensated interim receiver with general receiver powers except selling or liquidating utility assets until judicial review and court ruling on the receivership petition.

headings.title: Final commission determination attached to court petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires attaching an official copy of the commission's subsection 1 determination to the circuit court petition and prohibits filing until that determination is final and unappealable.

headings.title: Service of summons by personal delivery or posting
headings.reviewNote: Establishes five-day personal service of summons and petition, plus optional conspicuous posting on the utility system and ordinary and certified mail ten days before the return date or via alias summons.

headings.title: Court appointment of receiver and default notice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court after hearing to appoint a responsible, knowledgeable receiver and requires certified mail notice of default judgments to the defendant.

headings.title: Receiver bond, duties, compensation, and civil immunity
headings.reviewNote: Requires a receiver bond, grants attachment-receiver powers and court-determined compensation from utility assets, and provides personal civil liability immunity except for intentional, wanton, willful, or grossly negligent conduct.

headings.title: Duration of receivership and asset sale or liquidation
headings.reviewNote: Continues receiver control until return to owners serves customer best interests, or directs the receiver after hearing to transfer by sale or liquidate utility assets.

headings.title: Receivership cumulative to other legal remedies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that appointment of a receiver or interim receiver is in addition to any other remedies provided by law.

headings.title: Use of collected violation penalties for utility operations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts, notwithstanding section 386.600, to order PSC violation penalties collected from a small water or sewer corporation in receivership to be used to support its operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to petition circuit court to place small water or sewer utilities serving 8,000 or fewer connections into receivership, interim receiver appointments, service of summons, receiver duties and immunity, liquidation, and penalty use.

headings.title: Definitions of capable utility and small corporations
headings.reviewNote: Defines capable public utility, department, small sewer corporation, and small water corporation, noting the source footnote that 'Article IV' appears in original rolls for Article VI.

headings.title: Grounds for ordering acquisition by capable utility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission after notice and hearing to order a capable public utility to acquire a small water or sewer corporation for safety/adequacy violations, noncompliance with orders, inability to serve, impractical alternatives, and acquirer capability.

headings.title: Mandatory discussion of alternatives to acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission, except upon imminent threat of serious harm to life or property, to discuss alternatives and give the small utility thirty days to investigate reorganization, operation contracts, merger, or public acquisition.

headings.title: Interim receiver for imminent threat of serious harm
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to appoint an interim receiver prior to hearing upon determining an imminent threat of serious harm to life or property, with a hearing as soon as practicable thereafter.

headings.title: Mandatory factors considered in acquisition determination
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to consider the small utility's capabilities, proximate utility alternatives, needed improvement expenditures, service area expansion potential, and Department of Natural Resources advice.

headings.title: Acquisition order and certificate of convenience
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission after a subsection 2 determination to issue an acquisition order granting a certificate of public convenience and necessity for the established service area.

headings.title: Determination of acquisition price and rate base
headings.reviewNote: Provides for acquisition price by commission-approved agreement or commission-determined ratemaking rate base after notice and hearing, with the small utility bearing the burden of establishing rate base.

headings.title: Submission and approval of compliance improvement plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the acquiring utility within thirty days after acquisition to submit a compliance improvement plan and timetable to the commission and Department of Natural Resources for comment and expeditious approval.

headings.title: Civil damages immunity during approved improvement plan
headings.reviewNote: Shields the acquiring capable public utility from damages proximately caused by the small utility's prior violations while complying with an approved plan, subject to timetable, noncompliance, and sixty-day DNR objection exceptions.

headings.title: Enforcement action immunity during approved improvement plan
headings.reviewNote: Shields the acquiring utility from state or local enforcement actions by notified agencies for prior violations while complying with an approved plan, except beyond the timetable, on noncompliance, upon DNR objection, or for emergency advisories.

headings.title: Small company rate case procedure and return adder
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to authorize using small company rate case procedures for up to three years with a one hundred basis point return adder on acquired and improved ratemaking rate base.

headings.title: Standing to initiate complaint and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission staff, public counsel, local officials, or at least twenty-five consumers or prospective consumers to initiate acquisition complaints, placing the public interest burden of proof on the complainant.

headings.title: Service of notice on parties and utility customers
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving notice on the small utility, public counsel, Department of Natural Resources, proximate utilities and municipalities, and served municipalities, and directing customer notice.

headings.title: Petition for capable utility designation by smaller utility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a public utility with fewer than eight thousand connections to petition for designation as a capable public utility regardless of proximity if not detrimental to the public interest.

headings.title: Use of receivership penalties to reduce purchase price
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts, notwithstanding section 386.600, to apply receivership violation penalties to reduce the acquisition purchase price, with a corresponding commission reduction in ratemaking rate base.

headings.title: Rulemaking initiation and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to initiate rulemaking by June 29, 2005, subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2005.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to order capable public utilities to acquire small water or sewer corporations serving 8,000 or fewer connections, alternative discussions, pricing, improvement plans, liability immunities, rate procedures, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Hearing upon rate schedule changes and suspension powers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to hold hearings on newly filed rate schedules, suspend their operation for up to one hundred twenty days, and afford parties prefiled surrebuttal opportunities.

headings.title: Suspension extension, burden of proof, and docket preference
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes extending suspension up to six additional months (operation of law date), places the burden of proof for rate increases on the utility, and requires docket preference and speedy decisions.

headings.title: Future test year election and post-test-year update
headings.reviewNote: Allows gas, water, or sewer corporations beginning July 1, 2026 to elect a twelve-month future test year unless detrimental to the public interest, requiring a base rate update within forty-five days after the test year with sixty-day party review.

headings.title: Bar on concurrent ISRS or WSIRA cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits gas, water, or sewer corporations electing a future test year from recovering test-year plant investment costs under ISRS or WSIRA mechanisms, noting the source footnote that 'sections' appears in original rolls.

headings.title: Rate base reconciliation and customer refund liability
headings.reviewNote: Requires reconciling future test year rate base within forty-five days after test year end and placing any revenue requirement difference from lower actual average rate base into a regulatory liability accruing WACC carrying costs.

headings.title: Business risk consideration in setting allowed return
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to consider any change in business risk resulting from implementation of the adjustment mechanism when setting the corporation's allowed return.

headings.title: Expense reconciliation and customer refund liability
headings.reviewNote: Requires reconciling specified test-year expenses within forty-five days after test year end and refunding lower actual expense differences via a regulatory liability without offsetting additional capital spending.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking by July 1, 2027, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to promulgate implementation rules by July 1, 2027 providing meaningful party review and disallowance procedures, subject to chapter 536 nonseverability after August 28, 2025.

headings.title: Definitions of base rates and revenue requirement
headings.reviewNote: Defines base rates (excluding statutory rate adjustment mechanisms) and revenue requirement for purposes of section 393.150.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to suspend utility rate schedules, extend suspension and allocate burden of proof, future test year elections and updates for gas, water, and sewer corporations beginning July 1, 2026, reconciliations, business risk, rulemaking, and definitions.

headings.title: Water and sewer infrastructure rate adjustment petition
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes water and sewer corporations serving over eight thousand customers to petition for a water and sewer infrastructure rate adjustment (WSIRA) capped at fifteen percent.

headings.title: Rate proceeding order prerequisite for WSIRA approval
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits approving a WSIRA for a utility without a general rate proceeding decided or dismissed within the preceding three years unless a new case is pending.

headings.title: Maximum collection period without new rate proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Caps the collection period for a WSIRA at three years unless the utility has filed for or is subject to a pending general rate proceeding.

headings.title: Restrictions on collecting dual infrastructure surcharges
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits utilities from concurrently collecting both an ISRS surcharge and a WSIRA, requiring rolling prior ISRS revenues into the initial WSIRA filing.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures for water and sewer corporations serving over 8,000 customers to petition for a water and sewer infrastructure rate adjustment (WSIRA) and collection limits.

headings.title: Submission of WSIRA petition and proposed rate schedules
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing proposed WSIRA schedules and documentation, serving public counsel, publishing commission notice, and submitting five-year capital expenditure plans three months before initial filing and annually by January 31.

headings.title: Commission examination and report and order timelines
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission examination of the WSIRA petition, permits commission staff to report within ninety days, allows a hearing, and requires an order effective within one hundred eighty days.

headings.title: Limit on frequency of WSIRA rate changes
headings.reviewNote: Limits a water or sewer corporation to effectuating a change in its WSIRA no more often than two times in every twelve-month period.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining pretax revenues
headings.reviewNote: Restricts commission determination of appropriate pretax revenues to seven enumerated factors including tax rates, capital structure, debt and equity costs, property taxes, depreciation, and prior WACC fallback.

headings.title: WSIRA calculation, allocation, and annual reconciliation
headings.reviewNote: Governs calculating and allocating WSIRA charges using tariff rate group billing determinants and base rate design, and requires annual reconciliation of WSIRA revenues against appropriate pretax revenues.

headings.title: Reset of WSIRA surcharge upon effective base rates
headings.reviewNote: Requires resetting the WSIRA surcharge to zero upon the effective date of new base rates following a general rate proceeding.

headings.title: Distinction from general rate increase petitions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that filing a petition to establish or modify a WSIRA does not constitute a request for a general rate increase.

headings.title: Prudence reviews in subsequent general rate cases
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that WSIRA approval does not bind the commission regarding prudence of infrastructure costs in subsequent general rate proceedings.

headings.title: Rate reasonableness and prudence review preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves commission authority to review the reasonableness of water or sewer rates and prudence of eligible infrastructure replacements under section 386.390.

headings.title: Business risk consideration in general rate proceeding
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to consider any change in business risk resulting from WSIRA implementation when setting the corporation's allowed return in a general rate proceeding.

headings.title: Promulgation of rules for WSIRA implementation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to promulgate rules implementing the WSIRA program subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

headings.title: Expiration of WSIRA provisions on December 31, 2031
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of December 31, 2031, for WSIRA provisions in sections 393.1503 to 393.1509.

entries.reviewSummary: WSIRA petition and capital plan filing, ninety-day staff report and one-hundred-eighty-day order deadlines, rate change limits, pretax revenue factors, calculation and reconciliation, prudence reviews, business risk, rulemaking, and December 31, 2031 sunset.

headings.title: Prohibition on deposit for delinquent residential customers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits regulated public utilities from requiring a deposit or guarantee for continued residential service from an existing customer delinquent at least five times in twelve months if timely monthly payments of at least $75 or 25% of a balance of $300 or less were made.

headings.title: Inapplicability to high balances or payment plans
headings.reviewNote: Exempts customers whose total outstanding balance exceeds three hundred dollars or who are making payments under a previously arranged utility pay plan from section 393.152.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibition on requiring deposits or guarantees for continued residential utility service from delinquent customers meeting monthly payment thresholds, and exceptions for balances over $300 or payment plans.

headings.title: Commission authority to phase in electric rate increases
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission in its discretion to approve a phase-in plan for electric rate increases resulting from significant capital additions.

headings.title: Phase-in for holding company FERC generation expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to phase in unusually large revenue increases for a PUHCA 1935 holding company subsidiary caused by FERC-regulated generation expenses of a sister subsidiary, with adjustments including reasonable financing costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Discretionary authority of the commission to phase in electric utility rate increases over multiple years with reasonable financing cost adjustments.

headings.title: Gas and water meter inspector appointment and duties
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to appoint gas and water meter inspectors to examine and verify the accuracy of meters used for public service.

headings.title: Prohibition on uninspected gas and water meters
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits corporations and persons from furnishing or putting into use gas or water meters that have not been inspected under commission rules.

headings.title: Appointment of electric meter inspectors and apparatus testing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to appoint electric meter inspectors and examine testing apparatus, prohibiting unapproved meter types.

headings.title: Utility testing facilities and apparatus maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Requires gas, electrical, and water corporations to provide and maintain suitable premises and testing facilities approved by the commission.

headings.title: Consumer meter inspection requests and cost allocation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes procedures for consumer-requested meter tests, allocating costs to the utility if inaccurate beyond specified tolerances or to the consumer if accurate.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and uniform inspection charges
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to adopt rules carrying out meter inspection provisions and establish uniform reasonable charges for testing upon complaint.

entries.reviewSummary: Statutory procedures for inspection and testing of gas, water, and electric meters, utility testing facility requirements, and customer complaint testing fees.

headings.title: Commission approval of innovative technology investments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to approve investments by electrical corporations in small-scale or pilot innovative technology projects like microgrids and energy storage.

headings.title: Definitions of electrical corporation and commission
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation and commission for innovative technology investment provisions, excluding certain nonprofit cooperative utilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to approve investments by electrical corporations in small-scale or pilot innovative technology projects, including microgrids and energy storage.

headings.title: Definitions of average and excess cost allocation terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines average and excess method, class cost of service study, commission, electrical corporation, and production plant costs.

headings.title: Revenue requirement allocation using average and excess method
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission in general rate cases to allocate production plant costs from fossil and nuclear generating units using the average and excess method or NARUC manual methods.

headings.title: Expiration of production plant allocation section
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of August 28, 2031, for the average and excess production plant cost allocation section.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for electrical corporations to allocate production plant costs in general rate cases using the average and excess method or NARUC manual methods, expiring in 2031.

headings.title: Growth project discounts for qualifying incremental loads
headings.reviewNote: Establishes five-year 35% discounts (300 kW to 10 MW, 45% load factor) and ten-year discounts (over 10 MW, 55% load factor) with a 120% variable-cost revenue floor, economic development incentive requirement, and under-utilized circuit bonus.

headings.title: Revenue allocation, qualification verification, and base-rate scope
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imputing foregone discount revenues, allocates discount impacts uniformly across customer classes, requires meeting load criteria within twenty-four months and annually thereafter, and restricts discounts to base-rate components.

headings.title: Definition of electrical corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation by reference to section 386.020 while excluding cooperative electrical corporations described in section 393.110(2).

headings.title: Termination of discount authority upon deferral expiration
headings.reviewNote: Terminates an electrical corporation's authority to offer discounts under this section on the date its deferral authority under section 393.1400(2) expires.

entries.reviewSummary: Growth project electric rate discounts for qualifying incremental loads of at least 300 kW or over 10 MW, revenue allocation and qualification monitoring, definition of electrical corporation, and expiration tied to section 393.1400.

headings.title: Gas growth project discounts for incremental loads
headings.reviewNote: Establishes four-year discounts up to 25% on variable base-rate components for new customers (at least 270,000 CCF annually) or existing customers (at least 135,000 CCF incremental annually) receiving government economic development incentives, subject to variable-cost and fixed-cost floors.

headings.title: Revenue allocation and ongoing qualification monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits imputing foregone discount revenues in rate cases after August 28, 2025, allocates impacts uniformly across customer classes, requires meeting criteria within twenty-four months and annually thereafter, and limits discounts to variable base-rate components.

headings.title: Definitions of gas corporation and variable base-rate
headings.reviewNote: Defines gas corporation by reference to section 386.020 and defines variable base-rate components as volume-based gas service rates excluding riders or surcharges.

entries.reviewSummary: Growth project natural gas rate discounts of up to 25% for four years for qualifying incremental commercial or industrial gas loads, revenue allocation and qualification rules, and definitions.

headings.title: Definitions of commission and electrical corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission and electrical corporation for large electric utilities with over one million Missouri retail customers.

headings.title: Qualification process for distribution system contractors
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations to establish an open qualification process and competitive bidding for distribution system construction contracts.

headings.title: Filing of verified statement and competitive bidding quota
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing verified compliance statements confirming competitive bidding of at least ten percent of external distribution installation expenditures.

headings.title: Exception for emergency projects and preexisting contracts
headings.reviewNote: Exempts emergency projects from bidding requirements and allows contractors not qualifying to receive guidance on qualifying for future bids.

headings.title: Annual commission report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to submit an annual report to the general assembly beginning December 31, 2020, on distribution competitive bidding effects and costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory contractor qualification and competitive bidding requirements for electrical corporation distribution system construction projects.

headings.title: Applicability to electrical corporations electing grid modernization
headings.reviewNote: Applies section requirements through December 31, 2023 to electrical corporations electing options under section 393.1400 with more than two hundred thousand Missouri retail customers in 2018.

headings.title: Three-year base rate freeze and force majeure exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires base rates to be held constant for three years from the prior rate case order unless a force majeure event occurs.

headings.title: Rate growth cap for pending rate case utilities
headings.reviewNote: Caps compound annual rate growth at three percent for electrical corporations with a pending general rate proceeding in 2018, imposing performance penalties for excess growth.

headings.title: Rate growth cap for nonpending rate case utilities
headings.reviewNote: Caps compound annual rate growth at 2.85 percent for electrical corporations without a pending rate proceeding in 2018, imposing performance penalties for excess growth.

headings.title: Reduction of adjustment mechanisms and deferral to asset
headings.reviewNote: Requires reducing rate adjustment mechanism charges under sections 386.266 and 393.1030 when necessary to avoid exceeding subsection 3 or 4 growth caps and deferring unrecovered sums to the section 393.1400 regulatory asset.

headings.title: Two percent growth cap for large power class
headings.reviewNote: Limits the large power service rate class average overall rate increase to a two percent compound annual growth rate and allocates reduced revenues uniformly across all other customer classes.

headings.title: Definitions of rate averages, force majeure, and class
headings.reviewNote: Defines average base, overall, and rider rates, class average base, overall, and rider rates, force majeure event (at least 3% revenue requirement impact), and large power service rate class.

entries.reviewSummary: Three-year base rate freeze, 3% and 2.85% compound annual rate growth caps through December 31, 2023, rate adjustment mechanism reductions, 2% large power class cap, and definitions for electing electrical corporations.

headings.title: Applicability to electrical corporations electing deferrals
headings.reviewNote: Applies beginning January 1, 2024 to electrical corporations exercising section 393.1400 options until their permission to make deferrals under section 393.1400(2) expires.

headings.title: Revenue requirement impact cap on regulatory asset inclusion
headings.reviewNote: Caps base-rate revenue requirement from section 393.1400 regulatory asset rate-base inclusion in rate proceedings concluded on or after August 31, 2023, excluding excess balances from rate base as a penalty.

headings.title: Definitions of revenue requirement impact cap and terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission, electrical corporation, rate-base cutoff date, revenue requirement impact cap (2.25% annualized over elapsed months), and subject section 393.1400 regulatory asset.

entries.reviewSummary: Revenue requirement impact cap on section 393.1400 regulatory asset rate-base inclusion beginning January 1, 2024, exclusion of excess balances as penalty, and definitions.

headings.title: Definition of electrical corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation by reference to section 386.020 while excluding cooperative electrical corporations described in section 393.110(2).

headings.title: Minimum investments in utility-owned solar facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations to invest at least $14M, $4M, or $3.5M (by customer size) in utility-owned solar facilities in Missouri or adjacent states between August 28, 2018 and December 31, 2023, with regulatory asset deferral above the 1% cap (noting the footnote renumbering 393.1030(2) to (3)).

headings.title: Deemed prudence and certificate of necessity exemption
headings.reviewNote: Deems compliant utility-owned solar investment decisions prudent and exempts construction from section 393.170 approval while preserving commission review of specific construction and ownership costs.

headings.title: Recovery of additional utility solar investments preserved
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not preclude electrical corporations from recovering costs of investing in or purchasing electricity from additional solar facilities beyond subsection 2 minimums.

headings.title: Expiration date and continued regulatory asset recovery
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of December 31, 2023 while preserving utility rights to recover remaining regulatory asset balances under subsection 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory electrical corporation investments in utility-owned solar facilities in Missouri or adjacent states from 2018 through 2023, prudence and CCN exemptions, additional solar recovery, and December 31, 2023 expiration.

headings.title: Solar rebate amounts, system limits, and utility caps
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations starting January 1, 2019 to offer solar rebates ($0.50/W through June 30, 2019; $0.25/W through December 31, 2023) up to 25 kW residential / 150 kW nonresidential, subject to annual and aggregate caps by utility size (noting footnotes on 393.1030 renumbering and 'commending' in original rolls).

headings.title: Recovery and deferral of solar rebate payments
headings.reviewNote: Permits electrical corporations to recover solar rebate payments through base rates or a section 393.1030 mechanism, defer and amortize over up to five years, and defer amounts exceeding the one percent cap to a regulatory asset with WACC carrying costs.

headings.title: Effective date and preservation of section 393.1030 rebates
headings.reviewNote: Makes solar rebates available effective January 1, 2019 and leaves section 393.1030(4) solar rebate provisions and commission orders unaffected (noting the footnote renumbering subsection 3 to 4).

headings.title: Classification of customer solar generation as conservation
headings.reviewNote: Classifies load reductions resulting from customer-owned solar photovoltaic systems as energy conservation for ratemaking purposes.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Grants the commission authority to promulgate administrative rules implementing solar program deferral provisions under chapter 536.

headings.title: Definitions of electrical corporation and commission
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation and commission, excluding certain cooperative electric utilities from section scope.

headings.title: Expiration date and continued regulatory asset recovery
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an expiration date of December 31, 2023, while preserving utility rights to recover remaining regulatory asset balances.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory electrical corporation solar rebates from 2019 through 2023 with annual and aggregate utility caps, rate recovery and deferral rules, conservation classification, rulemaking, definitions, and December 31, 2023 expiration.

headings.title: Alternative residential customer rates based on utility burden
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to approve alternative residential rates or bill discounts based on household utility burden with independent eligibility verification.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to promulgate rules implementing alternative residential utility rates subject to chapter 536 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to approve special alternative residential utility rates or bill discounts based on household utility burden, with independent third-party eligibility verification.

headings.title: Certificate of convenience and necessity for plant construction
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits gas, electric, water, or sewer corporations from beginning construction of any gas plant, electric plant, water system, or sewer system (except energy generation units of one megawatt or less) without prior commission permission and approval.

headings.title: Municipal franchise exercise and charter filing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires corporations to obtain commission approval before exercising any municipal franchise, filing charter copies and municipal consent statements.

headings.title: Commission hearing, approval conditions, and two-year expiration
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to grant certificates of convenience and necessity after hearing, impose reasonable conditions, and voids certificates not exercised within two years.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory certificates of convenience and necessity for constructing utility systems or exercising municipal franchises, with commission hearing requirements and time limits.

headings.title: Definitions of securitization terms and energy transition costs
headings.reviewNote: Defines nineteen terms for sections 393.1700 to 393.1715, including ancillary agreement, assignee, energy transition costs, financing costs, financing order, qualified extraordinary costs, and securitized utility tariff bonds, charges, costs, and property.

headings.title: Financing order petitions, elements, true-up, and advice letter
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes petitions for financing orders to finance energy transition or qualified extraordinary costs, establishes a 215-day decision schedule, 15 order elements, annual formula true-ups, irrevocability, issuance advice letters, refinancing, and survival through insolvency.

headings.title: Limits on commission treatment and utility discretion
headings.reviewNote: Bars the commission from treating securitized bonds as utility debt (except for income tax), revenue, or costs, excludes charges from section 393.1655 caps, preserves utility sole discretion not to file or to abandon issuance, and excludes bonds from capital structure and return.

headings.title: Electric bill disclosure and separate line-item requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires electric bills and tariffs to explicitly identify securitized utility tariff charges, assignee ownership, and separate line-item rates and amounts, while clarifying noncompliance does not invalidate bonds or financing orders.

headings.title: Securitized property rights, security interests, and true sales
headings.reviewNote: Establishes securitized utility tariff property as a present intangible property right, governs nonrecourse status and sequestration on default, and sets creation, Secretary of State perfection, priority, and true-sale transfer rules.

headings.title: Sufficiency of property descriptions in financing documents
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that descriptions of securitized utility tariff property in transfer agreements, security documents, or financing statements are sufficient only if referring to the financing order and stating coverage of all or part of its property.

headings.title: Secretary of state filing and maintenance of statements
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to maintain financing statements like transmitting utility filings under UCC Article 9 part 5, makes filing the exclusive method of perfection, and keeps statements effective until terminated without continuation statements.

headings.title: Missouri law governing securitized property rights
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that Missouri law governs validity, enforceability, attachment, perfection, priority, and exercise of remedies for transfers or security interests in securitized utility tariff property.

headings.title: State and political subdivision nonliability on bonds
headings.reviewNote: Declares that securitized utility tariff bonds are not debts or obligations of the state or political subdivisions, impose no tax or appropriation obligation, and must bear a face disclaimer.

headings.title: Securitized utility tariff bonds as legal investments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public entities (except PSC members/staff and OPC employees), financial institutions, insurers, and fiduciaries to legally invest sinking funds or other moneys in securitized utility tariff bonds.

headings.title: State pledge against impairment of bondholder rights
headings.reviewNote: Pledges that the state and its agencies will not alter, impair, or reduce securitized utility tariff property, charges, or bondholder rights until bonds and costs are fully paid, absent full compensation, and permits including the pledge in bond documents.

headings.title: Assignee and financing party exemption from utility status
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that an assignee or financing party is not an electrical corporation or electric service provider solely by engaging in transactions described in section 393.1700.

headings.title: Priority over conflicting attachment and perfection laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that section 393.1700 governs over any conflicting law regarding attachment, assignment, perfection, effect of perfection, or priority of transfers or security interests in securitized utility tariff property.

headings.title: Savings clause protecting prior securitization actions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that invalidation, supersession, repeal, or expiration of any provision does not affect the validity of prior authorized actions or securitized utility tariff bonds issued or authorized before that date.

entries.reviewSummary: Comprehensive authorization for electrical corporations to petition for financing orders and issue securitized utility tariff bonds for energy transition costs and qualified extraordinary costs, bill disclosures, property and security interest rules, state pledge, and savings clause.

headings.title: Definition of replacement resources
headings.reviewNote: Defines replacement resources to include enumerated renewable generation facilities, natural gas generation facilities, energy storage facilities, and enabling transmission facilities.

headings.title: Approval of replacement investment and deferral mechanisms
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission approval of replacement resource investments approximately equal to undepreciated retired plant investment (exempt from section 393.170), makes prudence binding, establishes dual revenue-requirement deferral mechanisms, excludes deferred resources from sections 393.1400 and 393.1030, and governs WACC carrying costs and rate-base inclusion.

headings.title: Concurrent 215-day procedural schedule and judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Requires a procedural schedule running concurrently with section 393.1700 financing order proceedings for a decision within two hundred fifteen days, with judicial review under sections 386.500 and 386.510 (noting the footnote that 'chapters' appears in original rolls).

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of replacement resources, concurrent approval and deferral mechanisms for investments replacing retired generating units alongside section 393.1700 financing petitions, and 215-day concurrent procedural schedule.

headings.title: Petition for retirement ratemaking principles and treatment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electrical corporations to petition the commission for ratemaking principles and treatment (including retirement date and useful life depreciation parameters) governing base-rate reflection of retiring generating facility costs.

headings.title: Deemed approval after two hundred fifteen days
headings.reviewNote: Deems proposed ratemaking principles and treatment approved if the commission fails to issue a determination within two hundred fifteen days of petition filing.

headings.title: Binding effect of approved ratemaking principles
headings.reviewNote: Provides that approved or deemed-approved ratemaking principles and treatment are binding for ratemaking purposes, subject to subsection 4 modification procedures.

headings.title: Monitoring major factors and modification procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires monitoring twelve categories of major factors and establishes forty-five-day notice, thirty-day concern, and ninety-day negotiation or commission resolution procedures for modifying approved principles.

headings.title: Interaction with securitization and replacement petitions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a determination under this section does not preclude petitions under sections 393.1700 or 393.1705, while barring base-rate reflection of costs funded by securitized bond proceeds.

headings.title: Retention of coal-fired generating assets in rate base
headings.reviewNote: Permits electrical corporations, if found just, reasonable, and necessary, to retain coal-fired generating assets in rate base and recover prudently incurred operating costs including at low capacity factor or offline for extreme-weather reliability.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for sections 393.1700 to 393.1715
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to promulgate implementing rules for sections 393.1700 to 393.1715 subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability after August 28, 2021.

entries.reviewSummary: Petitions for binding ratemaking principles and treatment for retiring electric generating facilities, 215-day deemed approval, monitoring and modification procedures, coal-fired asset retention in rate base, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Application for sole regional or watershed supplier
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes entities providing wastewater disposal or treatment services to apply to the department to be designated as the sole regional or watershed supplier.

headings.title: Contents and requirements of supplier application
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory contents for supplier applications, including metes and bounds boundaries, governance documents, financial statements, facility descriptions, and business plans.

headings.title: Operating restrictions within designated watershed area
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits constructing or operating competing wastewater facilities within an approved watershed area without an approved regional plan, exempting existing operators.

headings.title: Preference in department licensing and funding
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Natural Resources to give preference to designated regional or watershed suppliers in licensing, permitting, and loan and grant programs.

headings.title: Evaluation criteria for competing supplier applicants
headings.reviewNote: Establishes evaluation standards prioritizing applicants likely to provide stable long-term solutions and favoring joint applications from existing providers.

headings.title: Pricing and nondiscriminatory rates for wastewater services
headings.reviewNote: Requires regional and watershed suppliers to set nondiscriminatory rates with each user bearing a fair share of service costs, subject to utility rate laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedures for designating sole regional or watershed wastewater suppliers, application requirements, operating restrictions, regulatory preferences, and pricing rules.

headings.title: Commission authorization for transfer or mortgage of system
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission authorization before selling, leasing, mortgaging, or merging useful utility property, mandates filing political subdivision tax impact statements for county clerk distribution, and creates a conclusive nonuseful presumption for good-faith purchasers.

headings.title: Acquisition of stock or bonds in similar corporations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public utilities from directly or indirectly acquiring stocks or bonds of competing corporations without prior commission authorization.

headings.title: Thirty-day notice for small utility stock acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits acquiring or holding fifty percent or more of the capital stock of a water or sewer corporation serving 8,000 or fewer customers without notifying the commission within thirty days.

headings.title: Commission consent for delinquent small utility stock transfers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a small water or sewer corporation (8,000 or fewer customers) that is delinquent on annual reports or six-month assessments or violating PSC/DNR rules from selling or transferring fifty percent or more of its stock without commission consent.

headings.title: Preexisting stock, reorganization exchanges, and void transfers
headings.reviewNote: Preserves lawfully acquired stock and proportionate reorganization exchanges while declaring any stock transfer contract or assignment violating chapter 393 void and unenforceable on corporate books.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authorization for utility property dispositions and tax impact notices, restrictions on stock acquisitions, 30-day notice and consent rules for small water or sewer stock transfers, and voiding of unlawful stock transfers.

headings.title: Commission integrated resource planning proceeding duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission by August 28, 2027, and every four years or as needed thereafter, to conduct an IRP proceeding identifying reserve margins, environmental rules, alternative resource plans, and modeling standards at least eighteen months before first filings.

headings.title: Quadrennial integrated resource plan filing schedule
