headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission by August 28, 2027 to publish a quadrennial IRP filing schedule and requires electrical corporations to file alternative resource plans covering a minimum sixteen-year planning horizon.

headings.title: Required contents of integrated resource plan filings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies eighteen mandatory components of an electrical corporation's IRP filing, including existing portfolio details, generation attributes, rate impacts, hourly load forecasts, firm gas transportation, RFP/RFI results, preferred plan, and four-year implementation plan.

headings.title: Commission review, 360-day order, and balancing factors
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission after hearing to issue a report and order within three hundred sixty days (with 150-day utility cost updates) determining preferred plan reasonableness and prudence by balancing ten enumerated factors.

headings.title: Expedited CCNs, deficiency cure, and CWIP inclusion
headings.reviewNote: Treats approved preferred plan supply-side resources as necessary for 120-day limited-inquiry CCNs (noting footnote on 'and' in original rolls), establishes 60-day deficiency cure procedures, authorizes CWIP in rate base subject to refund, and preserves execution prudence reviews.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2025.

headings.title: Definitions of electrical corporation and planning terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation (excluding section 393.110(2) cooperatives), firm gas transportation, and generation attribute.

entries.reviewSummary: Quadrennial integrated resource planning proceedings and filing schedules beginning by August 28, 2027, sixteen-year planning horizons, eighteen required plan elements, 360-day commission review, expedited CCNs and CWIP inclusion, rulemaking, and definitions.

headings.title: Authorization and purposes for long-term utility securities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes utilities to issue stocks, bonds, or notes payable beyond twelve months for property acquisition, construction, service improvement, debt refunding, or five-year treasury reimbursement upon securing a commission authorizing order.

headings.title: Sewer corporation pre-1968 reimbursement and commission inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Permits commission consent to sewer corporation debt for pre-five-year income expenditures applied for prior to January 1, 1968, directs commission hearings and investigations, and restricts proceeds to order-specified purposes.

headings.title: Short-term notes and franchise capitalization prohibitions
headings.reviewNote: Permits notes payable within twelve months without commission consent (barring long-term refunding without consent) and prohibits capitalizing franchises above actual consideration, merger stock above combined par value plus cash, or consolidation/lease contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authorization for long-term utility securities and permissible purposes, pre-1968 sewer corporation reimbursement inquiries, and short-term note exemptions with franchise and consolidation capitalization bans.

headings.title: Accounting for disposition of securities proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to require utilities to account for the disposition of proceeds from sales of stocks, bonds, and notes and adopt rules ensuring use for order-specified purposes.

headings.title: Voiding of unauthorized or nonconforming utility securities
headings.reviewNote: Declares stocks, bonds, and notes issued without an authorizing order or nonconforming to required order provisions void, while protecting good-faith purchasers for value without actual notice from other order noncompliance.

headings.title: Corporate civil penalties for securities violations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects utilities issuing securities in nonconformity with commission orders or law, or misapplying proceeds, to a penalty of five hundred to twenty thousand dollars per offense.

headings.title: Felony penalties for officer and employee misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Deems corporate officers, agents, employees, or others knowingly issuing unlawful securities, making false commission statements, or misapplying proceeds guilty of a felony punishable by a $1,000 to $5,000 fine and/or two to five years imprisonment.

headings.title: State nonliability and nonguarantee of utility securities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no provision of chapter 393 or act thereunder obligates the State of Missouri to pay or guarantee any authorized utility stock, bond, note, or indebtedness.

headings.title: Voiding issues under pre-law authority without order
headings.reviewNote: Declares securities issued after the chapter's effective date under prior articles or votes void unless a commission authorizing order is obtained beforehand, and permits reasonable conditions.

headings.title: Retroactive approval for good-faith unauthorized issues
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to approve utility securities issued without prior approval if issued for section 393.200 purposes in good faith without knowledge of the prior-approval requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission accounting for utility securities proceeds, voiding of unauthorized or nonconforming issues, corporate penalties, officer felonies, state nonliability, pre-law authorization limits, and retroactive approval for good-faith issues.

headings.title: Commission power to ascertain property valuation
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to ascertain the value of utility property and all relevant factors bearing on value, and revalue property over time.

headings.title: Valuation hearings, notice, and written findings of fact
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes valuation hearings upon thirty days notice to affected utilities, requiring evidence to be written and verified in formal findings of fact.

headings.title: Conclusive effect and judicial review of valuation findings
headings.reviewNote: Provides for judicial review of valuation findings, making properly certified findings conclusive evidence of facts in subsequent proceedings.

headings.title: Supplemental valuation hearings for additions and betterments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes supplemental hearings and findings to evaluate new construction, additions, improvements, and betterments made after prior valuations.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to ascertain the value of utility property, hold valuation hearings on thirty days notice, make written findings of fact, and conduct revaluations.

headings.title: Commission power to require depreciation accounting
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission after hearing to require gas, electric, water, and sewer corporations to maintain proper and adequate depreciation accounts.

headings.title: Fixing rates of depreciation and depreciation fund expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to fix depreciation rates by order, requiring utilities to set aside depreciation moneys in a dedicated fund expendable under commission rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to require utilities to maintain adequate depreciation accounts, fix depreciation rates, and regulate depreciation fund reserves and expenditures.

headings.title: Commission supervision and authorization of utility reorganizations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects reorganizations of gas, electrical, water, and sewer corporations to commission supervision and prohibits reorganizations without authorization.

headings.title: Capitalization limits based on fair value of property
headings.reviewNote: Limits reorganization capitalization to the fair value of property, considering original cost, duplication cost, earning power, and cash payments.

headings.title: Mandatory agreement amendments conforming to authorized capitalization
headings.reviewNote: Requires reorganization agreements to conform to commission capitalization limits before becoming effective and authorizes imposing reasonable conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission supervision and approval of utility reorganizations, capitalization caps based on fair property value, and conditions imposed on reorganization agreements.

headings.title: Complaints regarding utility quality or prices
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes complaints regarding gas, water, or electricity price or quality, or sewer rates or efficiency, by municipal authorities or customer groups.

headings.title: Commission inspection of utility plant and books
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission upon complaint, through its agents, examiners, and inspectors, to inspect utility works, systems, plants, and methods and examine books and papers.

headings.title: Prescribed complaint form, contents, and signatures
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to prescribe complaint form and contents and requires signatures of complaining officers or consumers with their street and number residences.

entries.reviewSummary: Written complaints by local officials or at least twenty-five consumers regarding utility quality or price, commission inspection of facilities and books, and prescribed complaint forms and signatures.

headings.title: Notice and hearing on rate and quality complaints
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to give notice and conduct hearings on rate complaints, permitting corporations and complainants an opportunity to be heard.

headings.title: Order fixing maximum price or requiring service improvements
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission by order to fix maximum prices for gas, electricity, water, or sewer service, or order service and facility improvements.

headings.title: Three-year maximum price order duration
headings.reviewNote: Limits the duration of commission maximum price orders to a period not exceeding three years, except where sliding scales are used, and until modified.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining utility service rates
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission in setting gas, electric, or water rates to consider all relevant facts with due regard to a reasonable average return on capital actually expended and reservations for surplus and contingencies.

headings.title: Factors considered in determining sewer service rates
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission in setting sewer rates to consider all relevant facts with due regard to a reasonable average return on property value actually used in public service and reservations for surplus and contingencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission hearings and orders fixing maximum prices and service standards for utilities, consideration of return on capital, and order duration limits.

headings.title: Commission notice of utility rate increases
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to notify governing bodies of cities and counties imposing gross receipts taxes whenever utility tariff increases exceed seven percent.

headings.title: Mandatory reduction of municipal business license tax rates
headings.reviewNote: Directs cities and counties receiving notice to reduce business license tax rates within sixty days to match prior year revenues plus a growth factor, absent maintain order.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for commission notice to local governments when utility rate increases exceed seven percent and rollbacks of local gross receipts business license tax rates.

headings.title: Legislative intent to preserve local tax bases
headings.reviewNote: States legislative intent to preserve local tax bases, equalize tax burdens among energy suppliers, and restore revenue sources affected by industry restructuring.

headings.title: Funding local police, fire, and public health services
headings.reviewNote: Finds that municipal license taxes and franchise fees on gas and electric providers fund vital local police, fire, health, and equipment inspection services.

headings.title: Economic presence and competitive disparities in restructured markets
headings.reviewNote: Finds that sellers using local rights-of-way have an economic presence and that unequal tax burdens create unfair competition and municipal revenue losses.

headings.title: Public health and safety registration of energy sellers
headings.reviewNote: Finds electricity and gas to be essential but dangerous commodities requiring registration of all energy sellers to protect public health and safety.

headings.title: Interstate commerce preemption disclaimer
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections do not intend to regulate interstate pipeline transportation in violation of federal preemption.

entries.reviewSummary: Legislative findings and intent regarding energy taxation, preserving local tax bases, equalizing tax burdens, and registering retail gas and electric suppliers.

headings.title: Seller certification and business license tax agreements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits non-distributor persons from providing energy services in political subdivisions with business license taxes unless certified by the commission as a seller and filing an agreement to pay applicable taxes, and bars distributors from serving uncertified sellers.

headings.title: Franchise fee and PILOT agreements for energy sellers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits providing energy services where a franchise agreement or municipal distribution system exists unless the seller contracts with the political subdivision or obtains commission certification and agrees to pay its proportionate franchise fee or PILOT.

headings.title: Challenge waivers, declaratory actions, and audit access
headings.reviewNote: Requires seller agreements to waive validity and refund challenges, allows standing declaratory judgment actions without signing, and limits agreements to payment obligations and record/audit availability.

headings.title: Commission certification procedures under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to establish seller certification procedures pursuant to chapter 536.

headings.title: Limitation on use of rights-of-way and distribution systems
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section confers no seller right to use distributor or political subdivision rights-of-way, easements, or distribution systems except to provide energy services to retail customers.

headings.title: Termination of agreements upon breach and hearing procedure
headings.reviewNote: Terminates agreements upon material breach, requires fifteen-day hearing requests after notice, and prohibits seller and distributor energy services thirty days after an adverse commission breach determination.

headings.title: Rate parity cap with distributor taxes and fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers to pay political subdivisions at a rate equal to but not greater than the rate paid by a distributor for business license taxes, franchise fees, or PILOTs.

headings.title: No conferred service rights and gas seller filing
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section confers no right to provide energy services absent compliance with all applicable laws and commission rules, and requires natural gas sellers to file agreements within thirty days of passage.

headings.title: Tax credit for taxes paid in other jurisdictions
headings.reviewNote: Grants a credit against section 393.299 taxes upon proof of taxes legally due and paid in another state or political subdivision on the same energy sale or transfer.

headings.title: Nonseverability clause notwithstanding section 1.140
headings.reviewNote: Declares section 393.299 nonseverable notwithstanding section 1.140, invalidating all remaining provisions if any provision is held invalid.

entries.reviewSummary: Certification and tax/franchise/PILOT payment agreements required for non-distributor retail energy sellers, mandatory challenge waivers, chapter 536 certification procedures, breach hearings, rate parity, multistate tax credits, and nonseverability.

headings.title: Customer utility bills in Braille or bold print
headings.reviewNote: Requires any public or private provider of telephone, sewer, water, electric, or gas utility service, upon customer request, to provide bills in Braille or at least twenty-four point bold-faced type print or both.

headings.title: Effective date of August 28, 1999
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an effective date of August 28, 1999 for section 393.300.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirement that public and private utility providers furnish customer bills in Braille or twenty-four point bold-faced type upon request, effective August 28, 1999.

headings.title: Notice of legal challenge and agreement suspension
headings.reviewNote: Requires any party challenging a section 393.299 agreement to furnish the initial pleading to the commission, immediately suspending the agreement pending final judgment, and bars energy services after commission notice.

headings.title: Effect of invalidation of section 393.299 and no refunds
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits energy services if section 393.299 is declared invalid except upon a public convenience and necessity finding and full chapter compliance, and bars tax or fee refunds to sellers signing validity waivers.

entries.reviewSummary: Automatic suspension of section 393.299 seller agreements upon court challenge and commission notice, and consequences if section 393.299 is held invalid.

headings.title: Applicability limited to gas corporations and school aggregation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts section application to gas corporations providing service under the experimental school natural gas aggregation program.

headings.title: Definitions of aggregate, commission, and eligible school entity
headings.reviewNote: Defines aggregate, commission, and eligible school entity to include urban, metropolitan, charter, private, and parochial school districts.

headings.title: Filing of experimental aggregation tariffs for school districts
headings.reviewNote: Requires gas corporations to file experimental tariffs by August 1, 2002, allowing eligible school entities to aggregate natural gas purchases.

headings.title: Mandatory provisions of school natural gas aggregation tariffs
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory tariff terms, including pass-through of gas and transportation costs, aggregation fees capped at 0.4 cents per therm, and meter thresholds.

headings.title: Commission suspension and approval of aggregation tariffs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to review and approve aggregation tariffs upon finding no negative financial impact on utilities or taxing authorities.

headings.title: Treatment of pipeline capacity costs for school entities
headings.reviewNote: Directs that pipeline capacity costs for participating schools be treated consistently with large industrial and commercial transportation customers.

headings.title: Extension of experimental tariffs until terminated by commission
headings.reviewNote: Extends experimental aggregation tariffs in effect as of August 28, 2005, until affirmatively terminated by the commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Experimental tariffs allowing public, private, and parochial school entities to aggregate natural gas purchases and pipeline transportation, with cost protections and tariff extensions.

headings.title: Definitions of large and small water utilities
headings.reviewNote: Defines large water public utility and small water utility serving eight thousand or fewer customer connections.

headings.title: Election of statutory ratemaking rate base appraisal procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes large water public utilities to elect statutory appraisal procedures to determine the ratemaking rate base of acquired small water or sewer utilities.

headings.title: Appointment and duties of certified general appraisers
headings.reviewNote: Requires an appraisal by at least two disinterested certified general appraisers (one appointed by each utility, with a third optionally appointed by the commission) under USPAP, valid when signed by two of three appraisers.

headings.title: Right to decline acquisition and purchase price distinction
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that parties retain the right to decline acquisitions and that appraisals do not establish mandatory final purchase prices.

headings.title: Calculation of ratemaking rate base upon acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Establishes formulas for calculating the ratemaking rate base as the lesser of purchase price or appraised value plus transaction and improvement costs.

headings.title: Consolidation into acquiring utility existing service area
headings.reviewNote: Requires the acquired small water utility to become part of an existing contiguous, closest, or best-suited service area of the acquiring large water public utility for ratemaking purposes upon acquisition.

headings.title: Permit compliance plans and continued customer service
headings.reviewNote: Requires new permits under chapters 640 and 644 to include a plan resolving outstanding permit compliance issues and requires continuing service to all customers served at the time of sale.

headings.title: Exclusive scope and independent public interest review
headings.reviewNote: Limits section 393.320 exclusively to small water utility acquisitions, requires independent commission public-interest determination regardless of ratepayer votes, and excludes electric, gas, and other utilities.

headings.title: Commission rulemaking authority for utility acquisitions
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the commission to implement small water and sewer utility acquisition procedures under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Appraisal and valuation procedures for large water public utilities acquiring small water or sewer utilities, ratemaking rate base calculation, service area consolidation, permit compliance plans, scope limits, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Definitions of electrical corporation and qualifying facility
headings.reviewNote: Defines electrical corporation (excluding section 393.110(2) cooperatives) and facility (primary metals processing, steel production/fabrication NAICS 331110, or new/incremental load of at least 50 MW monthly demand).

headings.title: Authorization of special non-cost-of-service electric rates
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission outside a general rate proceeding to approve special rates for qualifying facilities upon finding the facility would not otherwise commence operations, state interest, uniform base-rate allocation of reduced revenues, and a tracking mechanism.

headings.title: Net margin tracking mechanism and regulatory deferral
headings.reviewNote: Requires special rate orders to establish a retroactive net margin tracking mechanism keeping utility net income neutral and deferring net margin changes to a regulatory asset or liability amortized in general rate proceedings.

headings.title: Authority to serve facilities inside or outside territory
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes electrical corporations, notwithstanding section 393.170, to serve qualifying facilities under commission-approved special rate schedules, treating outside-territory facilities as within certificated territory.

headings.title: Written application, ten-year duration, and commission conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires written application by the utility or outside-territory facility specifying requested terms, limits special rate duration to ten years, and authorizes commission conditions.

headings.title: Eligibility to reapply for special electric rate
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any entity previously granted a special rate under section 393.355 to reapply to the commission for a special rate.

entries.reviewSummary: Commission authority to approve special non-cost-of-service electric rates for primary metals, steel, or 50 MW incremental load facilities, net margin tracking, outside-territory service, ten-year duration, and reapplication.

headings.title: Definitions of commission and water corporation
headings.reviewNote: Defines commission and water corporation (a corporation with more than one thousand Missouri customers meeting section 386.020).

headings.title: Contractor qualification and competitive bidding process
headings.reviewNote: Requires water corporations to establish an open contractor qualification and lowest-and-best competitive bidding process for planned distribution infrastructure projects, with feedback for nonqualifying contractors and exceptions for employees, emergencies, and preexisting contracts.

headings.title: Compliance statements and twenty percent bidding threshold
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing compliance statements within thirty days after August 28, 2018 and with general rate filings confirming use of the qualification process for at least twenty percent of external planned distribution project expenditures.

headings.title: Commission report to general assembly by December 2020
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to submit a report to the general assembly by December 31, 2020 on water corporation compliance and comparative costs of planned infrastructure projects.

entries.reviewSummary: Contractor qualification and competitive bidding requirements for water corporations with over 1,000 customers on planned distribution infrastructure projects, 20% external expenditure compliance statements, and 2020 legislative report.

headings.title: Incorporation of section 386.020 definitions
headings.reviewNote: Applies the definitions of words, phrases, and terms in section 386.020 to section 393.400.

headings.title: Deferral of state and local property tax differences
headings.reviewNote: Requires electric, gas, sewer, and water corporations to defer differences between actual and base-rate state or local property tax expenses to a regulatory asset or liability account for amortization, rate-base adjustment, and prudence review in subsequent rate cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Incorporation of section 386.020 definitions and mandatory deferral of state and local property tax expense differences to a regulatory asset or liability account for electric, gas, sewer, and water corporations.

headings.title: Definitions of power plant closure and resource terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines dispatchable power resource, electrical corporation, existing electric generating power plant (over 100 MW thermal), regional transmission operator, reliable electric generation, and unexpected or unplanned cause or event.

headings.title: Prior certification of replacement accredited reliable capacity
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations prior to closing an existing Missouri power plant on or after January 1, 2026 to certify securing equal or greater summer-winter average accredited capacity with at least eighty percent dispatchable power resources.

headings.title: Concurrent operation, unplanned closures, and settlement restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires concurrent operation (or within 180 days when reusing interconnection facilities), establishes a 120-day application and 270-day commission order process for unexpected closures with interim firm capacity, and restricts voluntary closure settlements.

headings.title: Accredited capacity verification and loss-of-load exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires matching summer-winter accredited capacity as of the section 393.170 application, authorizes considering RTO loss-of-load data, and waives subsection 2 if significant long-term load loss makes full replacement contrary to the public interest.

headings.title: Geographic siting in Missouri or neighboring states
headings.reviewNote: Permits constructing replacement reliable electric generation in Missouri or a neighboring state connected to the utility's RTO grid or a seam-sharing RTO operating in Missouri.

headings.title: Certification to commission, general assembly, and governor
headings.reviewNote: Requires electrical corporations on or before the replacement generation's in-service date to certify compliance with section 393.401 to the commission, general assembly, and governor.

headings.title: Exclusion from section 393.1705 replacement resources
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits existing power plant capacity replaced under section 393.401 from being replaced by replacement resources under section 393.1705.

entries.reviewSummary: Requirements for electrical corporations closing existing thermal power plants over 100 MW on or after January 1, 2026 to secure equal or greater accredited reliable generation (at least 80% dispatchable), unplanned closure procedures, loss-of-load exceptions, siting, and certifications.

headings.title: Affidavit for judicial access order to utility meter
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes utility companies upon customer denial of access to file an affidavit in associate circuit court requesting an access order for utility meters.

headings.title: Initial access order issuance, service, and automatic finality
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to issue an initial access order within seven days, requiring sheriff service, posting, mailing, and automatic finality if no bond is filed.

entries.reviewSummary: Judicial proceedings for utility companies to obtain court orders for meter access upon customer default, affidavit requirements, sheriff service, and finality timelines.

headings.title: Hearing request and bond requirements for customer
headings.reviewNote: Prevents an initial access order from becoming final if the customer posts a court-approved bond covering utility delay losses and charges within the order's time limit, entitling the customer to a hearing on the record held and decided within twenty days.

headings.title: Hearing proofs, burden, and automatic order reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the utility at hearing to establish a reasonable need for meter access under section 393.550(3) to automatically reinstate the access order as final, with both parties permitted to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.

entries.reviewSummary: Procedure for utility customers to contest meter access orders by posting bond and requesting a hearing, and judicial entry of final orders.

headings.title: Customer damages for willful and wrongful access action
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes awarding direct damages and reasonable attorney fees to a utility customer in default if the court specifically finds on the hearing record that the utility willfully and wrongfully instituted the access action.

headings.title: Taxation of court costs and sheriff expenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court in its discretion to tax costs and directs the court to determine which party must pay the sheriff's expenses referenced in section 393.559.

entries.reviewSummary: Award of damages and attorney fees to utility customers for willful and wrongful meter access actions, and court discretion to tax costs and sheriff expenses.

headings.title: Formation of joint municipal utility commission by contract
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes municipalities, joint municipal utility commissions, public water supply districts, and sewer districts to establish a joint municipal utility commission by joint contract to develop projects.

headings.title: Required contents of joint contract and governance
headings.reviewNote: Specifies eleven mandatory joint contract provisions including name and purpose, board of directors and optional executive committee, member-appointed directors and alternates, officers, majority quorum and voting, duties, adding members, financing, ownership, dissolution, and term.

headings.title: Successorship to prior municipal nonprofit entities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a commission, if the joint contract so specifies, succeeds to any prior nonprofit corporation, agency, or entity organized by contracting municipalities, assuming all contract rights and obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Formation of joint municipal utility commissions by joint contract, eleven mandatory contract provisions including board governance and voting, and successorship to prior municipal nonprofit entities.

headings.title: Enumerated corporate and public powers of commission
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates extensive corporate, municipal, and public powers of joint municipal utility commissions, including eminent domain, bonding, and rate setting.

headings.title: Continued water service outside municipality boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes joint municipal utility commissions purchasing private water utilities to continue and expand water service outside municipal boundaries.

headings.title: Successor service rights to nonprofit water entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commissions succeeding nonprofit water or sewer corporations to continue and expand service in previously served territories with specified exclusions.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerated statutory powers of joint municipal utility commissions, eminent domain authority, rate setting, and extraterritorial water service rights.

headings.title: Revenue bonds payable solely from net revenues
headings.reviewNote: Directs that revenue bonds issued by joint municipal utility commissions shall be payable solely from project net revenues or nontax funds.

headings.title: Statement of nonliability of state and municipalities
headings.reviewNote: Requires bonds to recite that they are special obligations of the commission and not debts of the state or contracting municipalities.

headings.title: Bond issuance purposes, reserves, and interest costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes issuing revenue bonds to acquire, construct, or improve projects, establish reserves, and pay construction period interest.

headings.title: Bond resolution, form, terms, and redemption
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that bonds may be issued under resolution or trust indenture in series with terms, maturities, and redemption provisions fixed by the board.

headings.title: Sale of bonds at public or private sale
headings.reviewNote: Permits selling revenue bonds at public or private sale at prices determined by the commission.

headings.title: Manual or facsimile signatures and validity after departure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes manual or facsimile signatures on bonds as determined by board or executive committee resolution, remaining valid even if signing officers leave office before delivery.

headings.title: Issuance of temporary bonds pending definitive bonds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a commission pending preparation of definitive bonds to issue temporary bonds exchangeable for definitive bonds when executed and available.

headings.title: Negotiability of commission bonds under commercial code
headings.reviewNote: Declares all bonds issued under sections 393.700 to 393.770 to be negotiable instruments pursuant to the Uniform Commercial Code of Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Issuance of joint municipal utility commission revenue bonds payable from net revenues, nonliability recitals, bond terms and sale, manual or facsimile signatures, temporary bonds, and UCC negotiability.

headings.title: Rate covenants in bond authorizing resolution
headings.reviewNote: Requires bond resolutions to fix project rates, fees, and charges sufficient to pay bond principal and interest, sinking fund, reasonable reserves, and operation, improvement, and maintenance costs.

headings.title: Bond resolution and trust indenture contract provisions
headings.reviewNote: Declares the bond resolution and trust indenture a contract with bondholders and enumerates thirteen permissible provisions covering security, funds, additional bonds, amendments, defaults, insurance, trustees, and paying agents.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory rate covenants in joint municipal utility commission bond resolutions and thirteen permissible contractual provisions in resolutions and trust indentures.

headings.title: Exemption of commission bonds and interest from taxation
headings.reviewNote: Exempts all bonds issued under sections 393.700 to 393.770 and all income or interest thereon from all state taxes except estate and transfer taxes.

headings.title: Taxation of commission real and tangible personal property
headings.reviewNote: Subjects commission real and tangible personal property (except properties acquired exclusively for water supply districts and commissions) to state and local taxation to the same extent as if directly owned by contracting or participating municipalities.

entries.reviewSummary: State tax exemption for joint municipal utility commission bonds and interest (except estate and transfer taxes) and local property taxation of commission property.

headings.title: Municipal bond elections, feasibility report, and public hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating municipalities to order chapter 115 bond elections only after receiving and approving an independent consulting engineer feasibility report under section 327.181 and holding published public hearings.

headings.title: Notification to election authorities under chapter 115
headings.reviewNote: Requires each participating municipality to notify the responsible election authority or authorities in accordance with chapter 115.

headings.title: Statutory official ballot form for revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the official yes/no ballot form submitting the participating municipality's maximum revenue bond amount and project description to voters.

headings.title: Majority voter approval and bond issuance
headings.reviewNote: Directs the participating municipality to declare the election result and cause the bonds to be issued if approved by at least a majority of qualified electors voting thereon.

headings.title: Municipal responsibility for bond election expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires each participating municipality to bear all expenses associated with the bond elections held within that municipality.

headings.title: Alternative three-quarters governing body vote for water facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an alternative three-quarters vote of contracting municipality governing bodies by ordinance or resolution for water supply and treatment facilities after a consulting engineer feasibility report and public hearings.

entries.reviewSummary: Municipal revenue bond election procedures, independent consulting engineer feasibility reports and public hearings, chapter 115 notice, statutory ballot form, majority approval, election expenses, and alternative 3/4 governing-body vote for water projects.

headings.title: Purchase agreements between municipalities and utility commission
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes contracting municipalities and other entities to enter into long-term take-or-pay purchase agreements with utility commissions to support bonds.

headings.title: Purchase agreement payments treated as utility expenses
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that municipality obligations under commission purchase agreements do not constitute general debt and are payable solely as operating expenses of municipal utilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorization for municipalities to enter into long-term purchase agreements with joint municipal utility commissions, take-or-pay terms, and debt limitations.

headings.title: Organization of nonprofit sewer companies by five persons
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes five or more persons to organize a nonprofit membership corporation to supply wastewater disposal and treatment services in Missouri.

headings.title: Execution and contents of articles of incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Specifies mandatory contents of articles of incorporation, including company name, address, duration, initial directors, and chapter 347 or 355 election.

headings.title: Department review of corporate documents and authorization
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting articles and bylaws to the Department of Natural Resources for compliance review prior to obtaining permits and after modifications.

entries.reviewSummary: Formation of nonprofit sewer companies, required contents of articles of incorporation, and Department of Natural Resources review and approval.

headings.title: Delivery of corporate articles to secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Requires delivering executed duplicate originals of nonprofit sewer company articles of incorporation, amendment, merger, or dissolution to the secretary of state.

headings.title: Filing and effective date of corporate articles
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state upon finding statutory compliance to file one copy of the articles in office records, making the incorporation, amendment, consolidation, merger, conversion, or dissolution effective upon filing.

entries.reviewSummary: Filing requirements for nonprofit sewer company articles of incorporation, amendments, mergers, and dissolutions with the Secretary of State.

headings.title: Qualifications and admission of company members
headings.reviewNote: Establishes qualifications for membership in nonprofit sewer companies and conditions for admission and termination of members.

headings.title: Annual meeting of nonprofit sewer company members
headings.reviewNote: Directs that an annual meeting of the members shall be held at the time provided in the company bylaws.

headings.title: Calling of special meetings of company members
